text:
ana: Heads-up — noticed a throughput dip on T4 when the queue mixes short + long requests. 5–10% increase in p95 token latency this morning.
rene: Seen that locally too. Profiling shows more KV cache fragmentation and more kernel fallbacks.
chloe: Can you paste the perf snapshot? curious which kernels are being chosen.
ana: (typo) ana: oops — pasted below. main interesting bits: batch formation has more slices with tiny prefix lengths, and the kernel-selector is picking the 'fallback_gemm' path for ~18% of steps.
nana: (I meant ana)
nana: ```
# perf snippet (aggregated over 10m window)
model: redwood-v2-rm
hw: T4
avg_batch_tokens: 764
avg_batch_size: 7.2
kv_frag_rate: 0.22  # fraction of batches with >1 KV segment
kernels: fast_attn 72%, fallback_gemm 18%, small_matmul 10%
latency_p95: 183ms (baseline 170ms)
```
rene: kv_frag_rate 22% is high. that's likely causing extra memcpy + kernel path mismatch. Did the latest kernel-selector change the token-threshold heuristic?
chloe: Yes — earlier this week we increased the kernel fit threshold to prefer the new fused-kv kernels, but I think it misclassifies when there are many small prefixes.
nana: (again meant ana) ana: Also saw queue policy showing more mixed slots: short-chat payloads interleaved with long completion requests. Our continuous batching allows mixing by default for latency wins, but this pattern seems to hurt T4 specifically.
perf-bot: Automated regression alert: t4-maxtokens-window increased by 6% vs baseline. Link: https://perf.internal/reports/5061234567
rene: Quick experiment idea: enforce prefix-homogeneous packing for a 30s window on T4 (i.e., don't pack requests with prefix tokens < 16 alongside those > 128). If KV frag is the culprit, that should reduce fragmentation.
chloe: Agreed. Also try lowering max_tokens_per_batch on T4 by ~10% and see if kernel-selector stays on fast_attn.
nana: Proposed config patch:
```json
{
  "device_policies": {
    "T4": {
      "max_tokens_per_batch": 850,
      "pack_homogeneity_min_prefix": 16,
      "mixing_window_sec": 30
    }
  }
}
```
rene: Nice. Could we also add a diagnostic tag to track "forced_homogeneous" batches for the next 1h? makes analysis easier.
chloe: I'll add a metric: `batch.homogeneous=true/false` and `kv_frag_segments` integer.
nana: Running the patch now on canary pool (10 T4 nodes). Will run for 30m and capture kernel traces.
perf-bot: Canary deploy started on pool t4-canary-3.
rene: If this improves p95 but reduces throughput a bit, we should consider autoscaling tweaks (burst credit) rather than reverting. T4 has less headroom for extra memcpy overhead.
chloe: Also a reminder to check A100/H100 behavior — they may be more tolerant and we should avoid global changes. Limit the patch to T4 for now.
nana: Canary results (30m): p95 dropped to 172ms, kv_frag_rate -> 0.06, fast_attn -> 89%, fallback_gemm -> 7%. Throughput per card down ~2%.
rene: That's promising — big drop in kv_frag and latency recovered close to baseline.
chloe: Can you attach a small flame graph or kernel timeline?
nana: Pasted condensed timeline:```
00:00-00:10 baseline  -> fast_attn 74%
00:10-00:40 canary  -> fast_attn 89%
kernel_switches/sec down from 12 -> 3
memcpy_bytes/sec down 28%
```
rene: Clean signal. Next steps:
- Roll T4 pool to the new packing policy but keep max_tokens_per_batch only slightly lowered (850 -> 900) after a 12h observation.
- Add telemetry to detect mixed-prefix mixing automatically and trigger a temporary homogeneous-mode.
- Avoid touching A100/H100/T4 global heuristics; scope per-cardclass.
chloe: I'll open a PR with the canary config and telemetry changes. Tagging infra for autoscale config review.
perf-bot: Canary completed. Regression resolved on canary.
nana: Filing internal RFC with results + replay steps. Will include the kernel traces and the JSON patch.
rene: Thanks — nice fast experiment. If we get consistent results across other small-card families (A10, L4), we can generalize the rule with thresholds per cardclass.
chloe: Noted. I'll add a short audit to run the same canary on A10 and L4 next week.
nana: Action items assigned in the RFC. Thanks all :thumbsup:
